clauses.current_legal_basis: The designation of the Department of State as Central Authority and the Secretary of State's authorization to perform the necessary acts in the order's own held text continue because the order states no end and the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches checked through 2026-10-14 found no instrument ending or amending it.
clauses.reason: The held text designates the Department of State as the Central Authority of the United States for purposes of the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, with no time limit or condition, and no held later instrument or machine-search disposition note amends, revokes or supersedes it, so the designation remains in force on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 12648 (53 FR 30637, August 15, 1988; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12648.txt) in full. The order has a single section: it designates the Department of State as the Central Authority of the United States for purposes of the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction and authorizes the Secretary of State to perform all lawful acts necessary and proper to execute the functions of the Central Authority. It states no duration, expiry or condition and rests on no authority statute that is cited as its source. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) report no instrument amending, revoking or superseding the order: the ofr_catalog search has zero hits; the U.S. Code and eCFR hits are leads only (the order is printed as a note to 22 U.S.C. 9006 and cited in the 1989 OFR codification) and are not relied on as a legal basis. The held-corpus search for the order number finds only the order itself and the 1989 codification SOURCE line. The single clause is therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14.
